source.stem:
The structure of a chlorofluorocarbon polymer is shown.

Displayed polymer structure: –C(CH₃)(H)–C(Cl)(F)–C(CH₃)(H)–C(Cl)(F)–

Which monomer is used to make this polymer?

packed_tags.topic: Mixtures, solutions, pure substances and separation

intelligence.enrichment: Handpicking separates solid materials from a mixture when the components can be picked out by hand because they differ in size, colour, or shape. Visible differences in size, colour, or shape make one component identifiable, so it can be physically picked out from the mixture. The learner correctly applies this rule: Handpicking separates solid materials from a mixture when the components can be picked out by hand because they differ in size, colour, or shape. Any solid mixture should be separated by hand if a person has enough time.
